Finding: Status tab counts don't reconcile with Total SPOs card: tabs sum to 37 (Open 12 + Drafts 5 + Scheduled 1 + Partially validated 0 + Validated 12 + Sent 6 + Paid 0 + Cancelled 1) but Total SPOs = 36.
Evidence: F01-list-cards-tabs.jpg; /contract-services header cards vs status tab bar
Recommendation: Make one source of truth. Either tabs are mutually exclusive and must sum to Total, or statuses overlap (e.g. Partially validated is a sub-state) and that must be stated. Reconcile counts server-side.

Finding: Summary cards duplicate 4 tab counts (Drafts 5, Open 12, Partially validated 0, Validated 12) and omit 4 statuses (Scheduled, Sent, Paid, Cancelled). Cards are a partial echo of the tabs, not an independent rollup; Validated 12 appears twice on screen.
Recommendation: Drop redundant cards or make them a distinct lens (e.g. $ committed, $ awaiting Accounting, overdue). Don't show the same count as both a card and a tab.

Finding: TEMP vendor codes and asterisk-prefixed placeholder names shown to users: '* Furtura USA Inc', '* MidAmerica Baptist Theological'; detail panel exposes 'Vendor code TEMP5493568100'.
Evidence: F02-list-table.jpg; F03 detail SPO Details panel
Recommendation: Hide TEMP codes from buyer UI; resolve/merge placeholder vendors to real records before surfacing. If a vendor is unverified, label it 'Unverified vendor' not a raw TEMP id + '*'.

Finding: Property name inconsistent: column shows 'Oakeigh Apartments' while scope text says 'Oakleigh Apartments' (and 'Oakleigh'). Vendor names look like junk/test records (e.g. 'MidAmerica Baptist Theological' as a cleaning vendor, 'Furtura' likely typo of 'Futura').
Evidence: F01/F02; SPO-848 scope text 'units at Oakleigh Apartments'
Recommendation: Canonicalize property + vendor master data; one spelling per entity. Add data validation on import.

Finding: Unit numbers are corrupted between description and structured field: desc 'Unit 303' -> field 'Unit 03'; 'Unit 101' -> 'Unit 01'; 'Unit 1906' -> 'Unit 0906'; 'Unit 1010' -> 'Unit 0101'; '308/1216' -> '0308/0216'. Leading digit dropped then zero-padded to 4 chars, so the structured unit no longer matches the real unit.
Recommendation: Fix unit parse/normalization. Units drive GL/property mapping and billing; a wrong unit mis-bills the wrong apartment. Validate structured unit against scope text; never silently pad/truncate.

Finding: Date column mixes relative and absolute formats in the same column: '24 hours ago' vs 'Oct 5, 2026, 1:59 PM' vs 'Sep 28, 2026, 7:31 PM'.
Recommendation: Pick one format. Suggest absolute date with relative tooltip, or relative <48h then absolute. Keep column scannable and sortable.

Finding: Scope of work repeats boilerplate already shown elsewhere: property address (in SPO Details / property), requester + date (in activity/meta), spend period (in SPO Details). The real scope is one sentence buried in repeated metadata.
Evidence: F03; SPO-845 scope 'At Oakeigh... clean Unit 101. Property address:... Requested by... Spend period:'
Recommendation: Scope card = the work only. Move address/requester/spend period to the Details panel (where they already are). De-dupe.

Finding: Vendor rejection does not stop or branch the flow. SPO-845 shows banner 'Vendor rejected this service order / Too busy' yet status = Open, stepper advanced past Sent to 'Awaiting invoice', and 'Vendor notification: sent'. Banner admits 'status and approval workflow are unchanged'. A rejected order is presented as awaiting an invoice that will never come.
Recommendation: Vendor accept/reject must be a real lifecycle state. Rejection should halt progress, set status to 'Vendor rejected / action needed', and surface Change Vendor as the only next step (not advance to Awaiting invoice).

Finding: Vendor acceptance is not a step in the 7-node stepper (Draft, Approved, Sent, Awaiting invoice, Map invoice items, Send to Accounting, Awaiting Payment). There is no node for vendor accept/reject, so the buyer can't see whether the vendor agreed.
Recommendation: Insert a 'Vendor response' node between Sent and Awaiting invoice (Accepted / Rejected). See proposed status model.

Finding: Order Activity ('SPO and invoice history') is empty on an SPO that was drafted, approved, sent, and rejected. No audit trail / no feedback that those events occurred.
Evidence: F03 page text: 'Order Activity / SPO and invoice history.' with no entries
Recommendation: Log every state transition + vendor response + document event to Activity with actor + timestamp. The audit trail is core to procurement.

Finding: Internal identifiers exposed to buyers: 'Vendor code TEMP5493568100', 'Location ID 656'. 'Vendor email recipients: jake@clkcorp.com' is the buyer/requester's own address, not the vendor's, so the recipient list is misleading.
Recommendation: Hide Location ID and raw vendor codes. Label email recipients clearly (who actually receives the PO). If no real vendor email exists, say so instead of showing an internal address under 'Vendor email recipients'.

Finding: Two 'Change Vendor' buttons on one screen (rejection banner + 'Manage this SPO'). Redundant primary actions.
Evidence: F03 (banner Change Vendor + Manage row Change Vendor)
Recommendation: One Change Vendor affordance. Keep it in Manage; banner can link to it.

Finding: Vendor picker returns '1-50 of 24,355' in a list labelled 'Approved, active vendors only'. Contains duplicates (EXPRESS CORPORATE HOUSING, LLC listed twice, identical address) and TEMP placeholders (* Furtura USA Inc). Many entries are leasing/housing companies, not service vendors.
Recommendation: Scope the picker to service vendors approved for this org/property; de-duplicate records; exclude TEMP placeholders. 24k results is not a usable approved-vendor list.

Finding: After selecting an approved vendor, 'Vendor email' is still required and auto-fills with an internal address (jake@clkcorp.com), not the vendor's. The selected vendor record carries an address but apparently no email, so the PO notification defaults to an internal person.
Evidence: F05/F06; ref 'Remove jake@clkcorp.com' chip on vendor select
Recommendation: Pull the vendor's email from the vendor record. If missing, prompt explicitly ('This vendor has no email on file - add one'). Never silently default the recipient to an internal buyer address under a 'Vendor email' label.

Finding: AI assigns unit codes that fail manual lookup. Units are 4-char zero-padded master codes (0101 = unit 101). Scope 'unit 1805' returns 'No units found' when typed manually, yet existing SPO-843 shows the AI mapped the same scope to code '0805'. Description unit and structured unit can disagree with NO warning - including on the Review step (desc 'unit 1805' vs Unit 0102).
Evidence: F08-unit-1805-no-units-found.jpg; F09 review desc 'unit 1805' vs 'Unit 0102'; SPO-843 rows
Recommendation: Validate AI unit picks against the property unit master; never truncate/pad to force a match. If no exact unit, leave blank + flag 'Unit not matched - select manually'. Flag any line where description unit != structured unit before submit.

Finding: 'Budget warning - review required' is cosmetic. Carpet-cleaning GL is 365% over its $850 October budget ($3,698.84 already spent before this SPO), yet the submit panel says 'No approval is required. Submitting will send this SPO to the vendor.' The warning neither blocks nor routes for approval.
Recommendation: Decide the rule: over-budget should either require approval (route to Order Approvals) or be an explicit acknowledged override. 'Review required' must map to an actual action, not a red bar next to a one-click Submit.

Finding: GL code dropdown is unsorted (6065, 6075, 6050, 6040, 6090, 6055, 6060, 6025...) and has near-duplicate carpet codes (8035 CARPET, 6040 CARPET REPAIR, 6035 CARPET CLEANING) that invite miscoding of the wrong account.
Recommendation: Sort GL list by code or group by category; show code+name consistently; collapse/merge ambiguous duplicates or add descriptions to disambiguate.

Finding: Property is fixed to the global 'Shopping for' context and cannot be changed in the wizard ('Change property in the top navigation'). Creating an SPO for another property means leaving the wizard to switch context first.
Evidence: F05 'This SPO is for ... Change property in the top navigation.'
Recommendation: Allow choosing the property inside Step 1 (it is the SPO's defining attribute), or clearly carry the draft across a context switch.

Finding: On Submit, SPO-854 jumped straight to 'Awaiting invoice' - Draft/Approved/Sent all completed instantly and the order awaits an invoice before the vendor has opened the email, let alone accepted. The lifecycle treats 'sent' as 'awaiting invoice' with no vendor-response gate.
Recommendation: Hold at 'Sent - awaiting vendor response' until the vendor accepts; only then move to 'Awaiting invoice'. See proposed status model.

Finding: Order Activity is empty on a freshly created+sent SPO (SPO-854). None of Draft/Approved/Sent/notification-sent events are logged, so there is no history even at creation.
Evidence: F10; SPO-854 Order Activity 'SPO and invoice history.' empty
Recommendation: Write creation, approval, send, and notification events to Activity immediately on submit.

Finding: AI line extraction drops ALL prices to $0.00 on multi-line scopes. SPO-855 scope stated $400/$400/$200/$600 explicitly; all four lines returned $0.00 and had to be priced by hand. (A single-line '$250' scope priced correctly, so it breaks when multiple per-line prices are present.) Total showed $0.00 for a clearly ~$1,600 scope.
Recommendation: Parse per-line amounts from the scope; if confidence is low, flag the line 'price needs review' rather than silently setting $0.00. Never let a multi-line SPO sit at $0 total with no warning.

Finding: The unit-price field parses whole numbers as cents. Typing '600' yields $6.00; you must type '600.00' to get $600.00. No currency mask, no hint. Trivial to create an SPO off by 100x.
Recommendation: Use a currency-masked input or treat the entry as dollars. Show the formatted value live and reject ambiguous input.

Finding: Splitting a line creates portions labelled as fractions ('1/2','1/2'), each requiring its own GL + unit, but the per-portion dollar amount is never shown (only the fraction) in the wizard or on the Review step. Could not reproduce the price zeroing out when splitting after a price was set, but the fraction-only display hides what each GL/unit is actually charged.
Recommendation: Show each portion's dollar amount (e.g. $300 / $300), not just '1/2'. Let the user split by amount or percentage, not only equal fractions.

Finding: The SPO detail 'Line items' table shows only Item / Unit price estimate / Total - it omits GL code, unit, and the split-portion allocation that the wizard Review and the list-row expansion both show. The allocation (the core of an SPO) is invisible on the detail page.
Evidence: F14-spo855-detail.jpg vs F13 review; SPO-855 page text line-items table
Recommendation: Show GL + unit (and portions) per line on the detail SPO tab, matching the Review step.

Finding: The coarse status badge stays 'Open' regardless of lifecycle. SPO-852 is Validated/'Ready for Accounting' (per the stepper and the list's Validated tab) yet the detail header badge still reads 'Open'. Same 'Open' badge appears on awaiting-invoice and rejected SPOs.
Recommendation: Drive the status badge from the lifecycle state (Awaiting invoice / In mapping / Ready for Accounting / Sent to Accounting / Paid / Rejected / Cancelled). 'Open' as a permanent label is meaningless.

Finding: Stepper node labels change between states rather than staying fixed and marking done. Pre-invoice: Draft/Approved/Sent/'Awaiting invoice'/'Map invoice items'/Send to Accounting/Awaiting Payment. Post-mapping (SPO-852): same slots read 'Invoice received'/'Mapping validated'. Comparing two SPOs, the same position shows different names.
Recommendation: Keep fixed node labels; express progress with done/active/future styling and dates, not by renaming the step.

Finding: Each line shows 'Original line estimate: $150.00' even when the current price is unchanged ($150.00 = $150.00). The 'original vs current' treatment fires when nothing changed, implying an edit that didn't happen.
Recommendation: Only show 'Original estimate (was $X)' when the value actually changed from the estimate; otherwise show one price.

Finding: Both vendor outcomes carry the same disclaimer 'The order's status and approval workflow are unchanged' - accepted (SPO-852, green) and rejected (SPO-845, red). The acknowledgment is purely decorative in both directions; acceptance earns no state change either.
Recommendation: Make vendor response consequential: Accepted -> advance to Awaiting invoice; Rejected -> halt + require Change Vendor. Drop the 'unchanged' disclaimer.

Finding: Property spelling inconsistent even within one SPO: data shows 'Oakeigh Apartments' but the stored invoice file is 'SPO-852-oakleigh-invoice.pdf' (correct spelling). Also the 3-unit repaint scope was extracted into TWO identical lines ('Full repaint of each unit; Units 101, 102, and 103' x2 @ $150), not 3 distinct units.
Evidence: F16-review-invoice-modal-validated.jpg; SPO-852 invoice filename vs property field
Recommendation: Canonicalize property spelling across all stores. Fix line extraction so repeated/duplicated identical lines aren't produced from a multi-unit scope.

Finding: 'Open' and 'Sent' are distinct statuses but the labels don't say sent to whom. The 'Open' tab filters status=issued; a separate 'Sent' tab filters status=sent. Newly created SPOs land in Open/issued with 'Email sent' + 'Awaiting invoice', so 'Sent' must mean something else (likely sent to Accounting), which the label never clarifies.
Evidence: list tab hrefs: Open->status=issued, Sent->status=sent; F01
Recommendation: Rename for the audience: 'Sent to vendor' vs 'Sent to Accounting'. Align the internal enum (issued/sent) with user-facing labels so one word doesn't mean two things.

Finding: The mapping screen shows 'Your work saves automatically.' and ALSO a 'Save draft' button in the same header - contradictory affordances (is it autosaved or must I save?).
Recommendation: Pick one model. If it autosaves, drop 'Save draft' (or show a passive 'Saved' indicator). Don't offer a manual save next to an autosave claim.

Finding: Two different invoice-review UIs exist: the standalone 3-step Invoice Mapping wizard (Vendor & invoice -> Match line items -> Review & validate, can span multiple SPOs) and the per-SPO 'Review invoice' modal (PDF vs extracted lines). Overlapping purpose, different layouts and entry points.
Recommendation: Unify into one mapping/review surface, or make their roles explicit (bulk multi-SPO mapping vs single-SPO confirm) so users aren't learning two tools.

Finding: SPOs have no presence on the home dashboard. Every card is order-based (Total Paid, Completed Orders, Open Orders 123, Invoices 49, Deliveries/Invoices to Validate, Approvals). The only SPO mention is one Recent Activity line ('Approval required: SPO-847'). A buyer can't see SPO workload (36 SPOs, how many awaiting invoice, over budget, ready for Accounting) from Home.
Recommendation: Add an SPO action tile to 'Needs your action' (e.g. SPOs awaiting invoice, mappings to validate, over-budget SPOs) and/or an SPO summary card, mirroring the Deliveries/Invoices to Validate pattern.

Finding: SPO approvals exist but are contradicted by the wizard. Dashboard Recent Activity shows 'Approval required: SPO-847 is awaiting supervisor approval', yet the Create wizard Review said 'No approval is required. Submitting will send this SPO to the vendor' even at 365% over budget. It's unclear when approval applies, who approves, and whether SPO approvals share the Order Approvals queue (Approvals 44).
Evidence: F19 Recent Activity 'SPO-847 awaiting supervisor approval' vs F09 'No approval is required'
Recommendation: Define the approval rule (threshold/budget-based) and reflect it in the wizard. If over-budget needs supervisor sign-off, the wizard must route there instead of claiming no approval. Clarify SPO vs Order approval queues.

Finding: Confirmed by live test: after the vendor accepted SPO-854, the only change was the green 'Vendor accepted' banner. Status stayed 'Open', the stepper stayed at 'Awaiting invoice' (where it landed on send, before acceptance), and the acceptance was NOT written to Order Activity (still empty). Acceptance, rejection, and no-response produce the same lifecycle.
Evidence: SPO-854 before/after acceptance; empty Order Activity
Recommendation: Gate 'Awaiting invoice' behind acceptance; log accept/reject to Activity with timestamp; reflect the outcome in status. Today vendor response is cosmetic.

Finding: Before any line is connected, 'SPO Total estimate' shows $0.00 even though the SPO line's $250.00 estimate is displayed right beside it, and the exact-match $250 invoice is flagged amber 'Invoice Total $250.00 - $250.00 over SPO total estimate' - a false over-variance. It self-corrects to '$250.00 / Matches SPO total estimate' only after you connect the line (or click Auto Map). So every mapping starts by screaming a false overage.
Recommendation: Base 'SPO Total estimate' on the selected SPO's own estimate (known: $250) regardless of connection state, or auto-connect 1:1 matches (see SPO-38) so the screen never opens on a false overage. If it must mean 'connected estimate', label it that way.

Finding: 'Draft saved' text and a 'Save draft' button appear together in the Step 2 header, confirming the autosave/manual-save contradiction from the landing screen.
Evidence: Step 2 page text 'Draft saved / Save draft'
Recommendation: Drop the manual Save draft or the 'Draft saved' pill - not both.

Finding: A single invoice line that clearly matches the single SPO line is NOT auto-connected ('0 of 1 invoice items connected'); the user must drag a connector or click 'Auto Map'. For a 1:1 exact match this is needless manual work.
Recommendation: Auto-connect obvious 1:1 matches (same amount/description) and let the user adjust, instead of starting at 0 connected.

Finding: Uploaded invoice shows '0.00 MB' for a 2.6 KB file (rounds MB to 2 decimals). Looks like a zero-byte upload.
Recommendation: Show KB for small files or more precision; never display 0.00 MB for a real file.

Finding: Per-line and total variance DO work once lines are connected: the 15%-over paint line shows amber '$460.00 / +$60.00 over estimate', and the footer shows 'Invoice Total $1,785.00 / $185.00 over SPO total estimate' ($60 over + $125 extra). Good. But 'SPO Total estimate' still reads $0.00 until the first line is connected, then jumps to the full $1,600 - so the screen opens on a false '$1,785 over' before any matching.
Recommendation: Keep the per-line/total variance (it's good); fix the $0 pre-connection baseline (SPO-36).

Surface: Invoice Mapping · extra invoice line not on SPO
Finding: An invoice line with no corresponding SPO line (Debris haul-off/dump fee $125) cannot be matched, so the flow stalls at '4 of 5 invoice items connected' with the confirm checkbox disabled ('Match each item, then check the box') and no SPO line to connect to. The only ways out are 'Correct Mapping' (delete the line - losing a legitimate charge) or 'Contact Support'. There is no 'accept extra charge' / 'add line to SPO' / 'code to GL without an SPO line' path.
Evidence: F25; checkbox stays unchecked at 4/5; F26-edit-invoice-items-modal.jpg
Recommendation: Allow invoice lines that exceed the SPO: let the user add a matching SPO line (with GL/unit + approval if over budget) or explicitly accept/booking the extra charge. Deleting real vendor charges to force a match corrupts the record.

Finding: The capable line editor (delete, Add line item, qty stepper, unit price, PDF side-by-side) is hidden behind a banner titled 'Extraction feels wrong?' / 'Correct Mapping', implying it is only for AI extraction errors. Users with a legitimately different invoice (extra charge, tax) won't think to look there.
Recommendation: Rename/relabel the entry so it reads as 'Edit invoice lines' generally, and surface it when there are unmatched lines, not only when extraction looks wrong.

Surface: Invoice Mapping · combined line can't map many-to-one
Finding: When the vendor combines two SPO lines into one invoice line ('Painting - Units 102 & 103' $800 for SPO items 1+2 at $400 each), the connector is strictly 1:1 - a second connection REPLACES the first. The $800 line can only attach to ONE $400 SPO line, showing a false '+$400.00 over estimate', while the other paint SPO line stays unbilled. The $800 gets coded entirely to one unit (0103) instead of split $400/$400 across units 0102 and 0103 - a real per-unit GL mis-allocation that the aggregate total ($1,735.20 vs $1,600, +$135.20 = just tax) hides.
Recommendation: Support many-to-one and one-to-many line matching (one invoice line splits across multiple SPO lines with per-target amounts), or guide the user to split the invoice line in the editor. A 1:1-only matcher cannot represent real vendor invoices.

Finding: Scout AI parsed tax: 'Invoice Total $1,735.20 / Includes tax $135.20 and shipping $0.00.' Good that tax is captured. But the SPO estimate carries no tax line, so tax always shows as variance ('$135.20 over SPO total estimate'). Tax needs a home that isn't a per-line overage.
Recommendation: Treat tax (and shipping) as invoice-level amounts compared separately, not as an overage against line estimates. Show 'Subtotal vs SPO estimate' + 'Tax' distinctly so tax doesn't read as over-budget.

Surface: Invoice Mapping · reworded lines not auto-matched
Finding: Reworded invoice descriptions ('Carpet steam clean - Unit 104' vs SPO 'Carpet cleaning, flat $200, unit 0104') are not auto-matched - every mapping starts at 0 connected and must be hand-connected, even when amounts and units line up exactly.
Evidence: F27 (0 of 3 connected); F20 (happy path 0 of 1)
Recommendation: Use amount + unit + fuzzy description to propose matches and pre-connect high-confidence ones; let the user confirm/adjust. The AI already extracts well; it just isn't matching.

Finding: Scout AI extracted ZERO line items from the clean exact-match invoice (INV-1003), showing 'No items found / No invoice items were found. Add them from the PDF.' - while the SAME engine correctly extracted the variance invoice (5 lines) and the messy-extraction invoice (3 lines, incl. tax). Retrying (Back -> Continue) returned 0 again. The easiest invoice forces 100% manual line entry.
Recommendation: Investigate why a well-structured invoice yields 0 items (table/format parsing). Add a visible 'extraction failed - retry' path distinct from 'no items on invoice', and make retry actually re-run extraction rather than returning the cached empty result.

Finding: Abandoning a mapping silently leaves a draft ('Continue where you left off - INV-1004...Resume'); starting another mapping for the same SPO creates additional drafts. Multiple half-finished invoice drafts can accumulate against one SPO with no way to see/clean them from the SPO itself.
Evidence: Resume prompt after cancel; multiple SPO-855 drafts
Recommendation: Show and let users manage per-SPO invoice drafts; warn before leaving an unsaved mapping; cap or label stale drafts.

Surface: Data model · unit codes vs resident unit numbers
Finding: Unit History shows the real unit master is building-based 4-digit codes BBUU (0101 = bldg 01/unit 01, 0216 = bldg 02/unit 16, 0301 = bldg 03). Scopes reference resident-facing unit numbers (101, 202, 1805, 1906, 1216) that do NOT map to these codes. The AI force-fits them: 'unit 1216' -> '0216' (a REAL but WRONG unit: bldg 02 unit 16), 'unit 1906' -> '0906' (building 09 doesn't exist). So mis-assignments can land on a real, chargeable, wrong apartment - silently.
Recommendation: Define the mapping between resident unit numbers and BBUU codes explicitly; validate every AI unit pick against the property's actual unit list and reject non-existent/ambiguous matches. Never coerce a unit number into the nearest code.

Finding: 'Scheduled' is recurrence, not a lifecycle state, yet it sits as a peer of the lifecycle tabs (Open, Validated, Sent...). A scheduled SPO ALSO has a lifecycle state - SPO-717 is 'Open / Awaiting invoice' AND in the Scheduled tab - so it is counted twice. With the two new test SPOs, Total is 38 but the tabs now sum to 39: the double-counted scheduled SPO is the off-by-one (SPO-01). The Scheduled tab even has different columns ('Next scheduled date', 'Schedule').
Evidence: scheduled list columns; SPO-717 appears in Scheduled + Open; tab sums 39 vs Total 38
Recommendation: Separate recurrence from lifecycle. Model the schedule (series) as its own object/section; a generated SPO instance carries the lifecycle state. Don't count a series as a status peer, so tabs reconcile with Total.

Finding: On SPO-717 the generic stepper shows 'Awaiting invoice' for the instance while a 'Scheduled SPO / Active' card describes the weekly series ('Every week on Wednesday 8 AM', 'Next draft 2026-10-07 - 2 slots consumed', 'Draft only: each SPO must be sent manually') with Edit series / Pause / Enable automatic sending / Cancel next occurrence / Stop. The series controls are good, but overlaying them on one instance's lifecycle stepper blurs 'is this status about this SPO or the series?'.
Recommendation: Give the recurring series its own page/section (cadence, upcoming/consumed slots, history of generated SPOs) distinct from any single instance's lifecycle. Link instances back to the series.

Surface: Data · unit code format varies by property
Finding: Unit codes are not consistent across properties: Cypress Lake uses 4-char BBUU ('0101','0216') but Oakeigh uses 2-char ('Unit 01','Unit 02'). Same field, two formats - compounds the unit-matching problem (SPO-48).
Recommendation: Normalize unit code format across properties, or make the matcher property-aware so it validates against each property's own scheme.

Surface: Detail · canceller shown as raw customer ID
Finding: The cancellation line reads 'Cancelled 9/30/2026, 4:06:19 PM by cus_01KSTGBKY9FK3G0G4VXEH8YFG5. test' - the actor is a raw Medusa customer id, not a person's name, and the reason ('test') sits inline. 'Scope: Only this SPO. Vendor cancellation delivery: sent.'
Recommendation: Resolve the canceller to a name/role; present reason and scope as labeled fields. Never show cus_* ids to users.

Finding: Spelling is inconsistent: the detail status badge says 'Canceled' (one L) while the list tab and status column say 'Cancelled' (two L).
Recommendation: Pick one spelling (US 'Canceled' or UK 'Cancelled') and use it everywhere.

Surface: Detail · stepper third label variant + no terminal render
Finding: A third stepper label set appears on the cancelled SPO: Draft / 'Submit for approval' / 'Send to vendor' / Awaiting invoice / Map invoice items / Send to Accounting / Awaiting Payment - different again from the pre-invoice ('Approved','Sent') and post-mapping ('Invoice received','Mapping validated') variants. And a cancelled order still renders all 7 forward nodes rather than a terminal 'Cancelled' state. The cancellation is shown as a banner and is NOT written to Order Activity (still empty).
Recommendation: Use fixed node labels; render terminal states (Cancelled/Paid) distinctly; log cancellation to Activity. Reinforces SPO-26/SPO-10.

Finding: A cancelled SPO offers 'Revive SPO' (un-cancel). Useful, but with no visible guardrail/confirm or audit entry, and given cancellation itself isn't logged, revive/cancel churn would be invisible.
Recommendation: Keep Revive, but confirm it and log both cancel and revive to Activity with actor + timestamp.

Finding: SPO lifecycle events generate almost no notifications. On /notifications the only SPO entry is 'Approval required: SPO-847'; there are NO notifications for vendor accept/reject, invoice received, mapping validated, sent to Accounting, paid, or cancellation - not even for the SPOs just driven (SPO-854 validated, SPO-845 rejected). Mirrors the empty Order Activity (SPO-10): SPO events aren't recorded or surfaced.
Recommendation: Emit notifications for the SPO transitions users must act on (vendor accepted/rejected, invoice received, mapping to validate, over-budget approval, payment). Tie them to the same event stream that should feed Order Activity.

Finding: Three different notification counts: the bell badge shows 10, the nav menu shows 'Notifications 20', and /notifications says '217 total'. Even allowing total vs unread, 10 vs 20 for the same unread set is inconsistent.
Evidence: F04 (nav 20) vs bell 10 vs F33 (217 total)
Recommendation: Reconcile unread vs total; show one consistent unread count on the bell and the menu, and label the page count as 'total'.

Surface: Notifications · low-value noise buries actionable items
Finding: The feed is dominated by near-identical 'Order #### confirmed / A new order was placed in your organization.' entries (dozens in a row), with no grouping, filtering, type tabs, or visible mark-as-read. Any SPO-actionable notification is buried.
Recommendation: Group/collapse repetitive order-placed events, add type filters (SPO / Orders / Approvals) and read management, and rank action-required items to the top.
